questions.question: A scene renders 800 separate Mesh objects, each with a unique material. What is the primary performance bottleneck?
options: Too many draw calls — one per Mesh object
Too many triangles in the scene
Textures consuming too much VRAM
JavaScript running too slowly on the main thread
questions.explanation: Each separate Mesh with its own material generates a draw call. 800 draw calls far exceeds the 200–500 draw call budget for most devices. Draw calls are typically the #1 bottleneck in web 3D — before polygon count or texture memory.

questions.question: When using THREE.InstancedMesh with 1,000 instances, how many draw calls does it produce?
options: 1,000 — one per instance
10 — one per 100 instances
1 — all instances are rendered in a single draw call
It depends on the polygon count of the geometry
questions.explanation: InstancedMesh renders all N copies of a geometry+material pair in exactly one draw call. The GPU receives the geometry and material once, plus a buffer of per-instance transformation matrices, and handles the rest internally.

questions.question: After creating an InstancedMesh and setting positions with mesh.setMatrixAt(), what must you do before the positions appear on screen?
options: Call mesh.updateMatrixWorld()
Set mesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true
Call renderer.resetCache()
Add mesh to a BufferGeometry first
questions.explanation: Three.js buffers instance matrices in a typed array on the CPU. Setting mesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true signals Three.js to upload the updated matrix buffer to the GPU before the next render. Without this flag, changes to instance positions are ignored.

questions.question: What is the key benefit of KTX2 / Basis Universal texture compression compared to PNG?
options: Smaller file size on disk only — decompressed at the same size in VRAM
Textures stay compressed in GPU VRAM, reducing memory usage at runtime
KTX2 files support higher color depth than PNG
KTX2 files load faster because they skip the JavaScript parsing step
questions.explanation: PNG textures are decompressed to full RGBA when uploaded to GPU memory. A 2048×2048 PNG uses 16 MB of VRAM. The same image as KTX2 ETC1S stays compressed in VRAM at around 0.5 MB — a 32x reduction in GPU memory usage.

questions.question: Geometry merging (mergeGeometries) reduces draw calls for static objects, but what is its main limitation?
options: Merged geometry cannot use textures
Merged objects can no longer be moved, hidden, or modified individually
Merging increases total polygon count
Only geometries with identical materials can be merged
questions.explanation: Once geometries are merged into a single BufferGeometry, the individual objects lose their separate identities. You cannot move, hide, or apply different animations to parts of a merged mesh. Use merging only for permanently static geometry like floors, walls, and terrain.
